verdict.label: Heavy review / verification
verdict.summary: Creating a custom Gmail OAuth app grants dedicated quotas, but sensitive and restricted Gmail scopes require Google OAuth verification and potentially a security assessment for production access.
verdict.cost: Free for Google Cloud project setup; potential third-party security assessment fees if storing restricted data on servers.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail that lets you immediately test and connect accounts without registering an OAuth app or undergoing Google verification.
whyOwnApp: To avoid sharing provider rate limits with other Composio managed app users.
To present custom developer branding and application name during user OAuth consent.
To request specific custom scopes outside of Composio's pre-configured managed app default set.

phases.name: Create Google Cloud Project & Enable Gmail API
steps: Create a Google Cloud project in the Google Cloud console.
Enable the Gmail API for your project.
phases.handoff: Cloud project created and Gmail API enabled.

phases.name: Configure OAuth Consent Screen & Test Users
steps: Navigate to Google Auth platform > Branding.
Enter App Name, User support email, and Developer contact email.
Select External under Audience and add explicit test user emails.
Declare required Gmail API scopes under Data Access.
phases.handoff: OAuth consent screen configured with test users.

phases.name: Create OAuth Credentials & Connect to Composio
steps: Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID credentials for a Web application.
Set Authorized redirect URI to <Composio callback URL from your auth config>.
Paste Client ID and Client Secret into your Composio Auth Config dashboard.
phases.handoff: Composio Auth Config created with custom client credentials.

phases.name: Submit for OAuth Verification & Security Assessment
steps: Complete app details, privacy policy link, and scope justifications.
Submit OAuth verification request in Google Auth platform.
Initiate third-party security assessment if storing or transmitting restricted scope data.
phases.handoff: Verification and assessment requests submitted to Google.

phases.name: Google Review & Verification Queue
steps: Google review team reviews OAuth consent screen and scope justifications.
Security assessment team validates compliance for restricted scopes.

phases.name: Publish App to Production
steps: Publish the OAuth consent screen to production status.
Note that public vs private setting cannot be changed after publishing.
phases.handoff: OAuth app is published and accessible to external production users.

artefacts.title: Google Cloud OAuth App Configuration Settings
artefacts.body:
App Name: My AI Agent Gmail Integration
User Support Email: support@example.com
Developer Contact Email: dev@example.com
Audience: External
Application Type: Web Application
Authorized Redirect URI: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Gmail Scope Justifications for Google Verification
artefacts.body:
Scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
Justification: The AI agent sends outbound email notifications and responses on behalf of the user when explicitly requested.

Scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly
Justification: The AI agent reads incoming emails to synthesize summaries and identify user actionable items.

artefacts.title: Google OAuth Verification Privacy Policy Checklist
artefacts.body:
- [ ] Privacy Policy URL is publicly accessible.
- [ ] Explains exact Gmail user data accessed and stored.
- [ ] Complies with Google API Services User Data Policy.
- [ ] Discloses data retention and deletion policies.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy URL
requirements.when: Required when configuring OAuth consent screen for External users and submitting for verification.

requirements.label: EEA Trader / Non-trader Declaration
requirements.when: Required when publishing listing for users in the European Economic Area.

requirements.label: Restricted Scope Security Assessment
requirements.when: Required if requesting restricted scopes (e.g. mail.google.com or gmail.readonly) and storing/transmitting data on servers.

requirements.label: Unverified App Warning / Test User Restriction
requirements.when: App shows unverified app warning screen to non-test users before passing OAuth verification.

scopes.purpose: Read, compose, send, and permanently delete all email from Gmail.
Read, compose, and send emails from Gmail without immediate permanent deletion.

redirectRules.rule: Redirect URI must match the callback URI provided in your Composio Auth Config.

blockers.symptom: Users see an 'unverified app' screen when attempting to grant OAuth access.
blockers.cause: The app requests sensitive or restricted scopes and has not completed OAuth verification.
blockers.fix: Submit a verification request in Google Auth platform or add user email to Audience > Test users.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio-managed OAuth app for immediate testing without unverified app warnings.

blockers.symptom: Redirects to error page with authError=invalid_client (The OAuth client was not found).
blockers.cause: Client ID configured in Composio is invalid, deleted, or mistyped.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact OAuth 2.0 Client ID from Google Cloud console into Composio Auth Config.
blockers.fallback: Re-verify credentials in Google Auth platform.

blockers.symptom: OAuth verification rejected or app fails review due to consent screen configuration.
blockers.cause: Publishing status is set to Testing or user type is set to Internal during public submission.
blockers.fix: Ensure user type is set to External and follow verification guidelines.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio-managed auth while resolving consent screen misconfigurations.

checklist.text: Choose between Composio-managed OAuth or custom Google OAuth app.
Create a Google Cloud Project in Google Cloud Console.
Enable the Gmail API in Google Cloud Console.
Configure OAuth consent screen in Google Auth platform > Branding.
Set Audience to External and add test users.
Declare required Gmail scopes under Data Access.
Create Web Application OAuth credentials and add Composio callback URL.
Enter Client ID and Client Secret into Composio Auth Config.
Submit OAuth verification request for sensitive/restricted scopes.
Undergo third-party security assessment if storing restricted scope data on servers.
Publish OAuth consent screen to production status.

uncertainties: Exact duration in days for Google restricted scope verification and third-party security assessment completion.
Specific redirect URI string matching rules (wildcards, port matching) for Google OAuth web credentials in provided documentation.

claims.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app option for Gmail.
claims.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes

claims.text: Using Composio-managed auth skips developer portal setup, client credentials, redirect URIs, and provider app review.
claims.quote: No app registration. You skip the provider's developer portal, client credentials, redirect URIs, and app review.

claims.text: Using your own OAuth app provides dedicated provider rate limits rather than sharing them with other Composio customers.
claims.quote: Dedicated provider rate limits. Some provider limits apply per OAuth app. On a managed app, connections share them with other Composio customers. Your own app has its own.

claims.text: Choosing your own OAuth app changes app ownership, branding, scopes, and provider quota, not token custody.
claims.quote: Choosing your own OAuth app changes app ownership, branding, scopes, and provider quota, not token custody.

claims.text: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration.
claims.quote: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration, but you only need to list scopes for apps used by people outside your Google Workspace organization.

claims.text: For security reasons, you cannot remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen after configuring it.
claims.quote: For security reasons, you can't remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen after you've configured it.

claims.text: If External user type is selected, authorized test users must be added to allow testing before publication.
claims.quote: If you selected External for user type, add test users:

claims.text: Google OAuth scopes are categorized into non-sensitive, sensitive, and restricted scopes.
claims.quote: Review the scopes listed in each of the three sections: non-sensitive scopes, sensitive scopes, and restricted scopes.

claims.text: Sensitive and restricted scopes require additional reviews to avoid unnecessary friction.
claims.quote: For any scopes listed in the "Your sensitive scopes" or "Your restricted scopes" sections, try to identify alternative non-sensitive scopes to avoid unnecessary additional reviews.

claims.text: Restricted scope usage requires a security assessment if restricted scope data is stored or transmitted on servers.
claims.quote: If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.

claims.text: The full mail.google.com scope should only be requested if immediate permanent deletion of threads and messages bypassing trash is required.
claims.quote: Note: Request this scope only if your application needs to immediately and permanently delete threads and messages, bypassing the trash.

claims.text: The gmail.send scope permits sending email on behalf of the user.
claims.quote: Send email on your behalf.

claims.text: The gmail.readonly scope permits viewing email messages and settings.
claims.quote: View your email messages and settings.

claims.text: The gmail.modify scope permits reading, composing, and sending emails without immediate permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account. This scope does not allow immediate, permanent deletion of threads and messages, bypassing the trash.

claims.text: Testing an app with public data access scopes before verification displays an unverified app screen.
claims.quote: If you see unverified app on the screen when testing your application, you must submit a verification request to remove it.
